issues_identified.title: SPDX header gap vs. LICENSE-CHECK.md gate
issues_identified.detail: LICENSE-CHECK.md §2.2 and validate.yml license-check job require SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later in every source file under source/. The git worktree commit df2f1ec (license transition) was merged, but the repo still carries the legacy AUTOGENERATED COPYRIGHT HEADER without the SPDX tag in the audited files. On the next PR that touches source/, the license-check job will fail unless the SPDX tag is added.
issues_identified.files_at_risk: source/obs/gs/*.cpp, source/obs/gs/*.hpp, source/obs/*.cpp, source/obs/*.hpp, source/util/*.cpp, source/util/*.hpp, source/ui/*.cpp, source/ui/*.hpp, source/*.cpp, source/*.hpp — full list in COPYRIGHT_AUDIT_REPORT.txt
issues_identified.recommended_next: Run a repo-wide SPDX header pass: append '// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later' to every source/* file, then verify with the license-check job locally before merging any new PR.

issues_identified.title: GPLv3 commercial-derivative blocker is real and must be re-confirmed before any productizing move
issues_identified.detail: LICENSE-CHECK.md §4 and docs/LICENSE_AUDIT.md both explicitly block GPLv3-derived code from entering the Nexus proprietary commercial tree. The fork is an open-source OBS plugin deliverable only. Any GTM plan that assumes a proprietary commercial build of StreamFX-derived code is blocked unless clean-room reimplementation or upstream relicensing is achieved.
issues_identified.recommended_next: Formally record the commercial-derivative constraint in a project decision record (ADR) and lock it to the GTM plan: LibreCast Studio is the open-source community face; any commercial OBS-adjacent product must be a separate clean-room effort.

issues_identified.title: 60 lainon attribution files need a clearer ownership/authorship narrative
issues_identified.detail: COPYRIGHT_AUDIT_REPORT.txt §Lainon files lists 60 files with a 'lainon' line in the copyright header. Those files span the shader, blur, color-grade, dynamic-mask, mirror, nvidia, transform, obs/gs, ui, and util subsystems. Whether lainon is a pseudonym, a contributor identity, or an automated insertion, the current attribution is ambiguous and should be reconciled before any public-facing author list or CREDITS file is finalized.
issues_identified.recommended_next: Cross-check git log --follow per-file to determine whether lainon corresponds to a real git author, a bot, or a stale header. If it is a real contributor, add to AUTHORS.md and CREDITS; if not, normalize the header.

issues_identified.title: CI validate.yml checks copyright presence but not SPDX-ID in the copyright.js gate
issues_identified.detail: The copyright.js step in validate.yml enforces the AUTOGENERATED COPYRIGHT HEADER presence, but it does not currently verify the SPDX-License-Identifier line. That enforcement lives only in the separate license-check shell step. If someone revises a file's header and drops the SPDX tag while preserving the copyright block, the copyright.js gate will still pass and the license-check gate is the only remaining defense.
issues_identified.recommended_next: Extend copyright.js to reject files that have the copyright block but lack SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later, or add a second node step in validate.yml that explicitly greps for the SPDX tag the same way the shell step does, so the gate is defensive in depth.

issues_identified.title: rt_safety_audit.py TARGET_FILES list is render/utility only — no audio TUs yet
issues_identified.detail: The script comment at line 66-69 explicitly says audio TUs are a placeholder for future Phase A3 audio integration. Today the gate only covers source/obs/gs/* and source/util/utility.*. If the fork later adds a real-time audio source or filter, the gate will not cover it until TARGET_FILES is extended.
issues_identified.recommended_next: Track the TARGET_FILES extension as a gated task tied to the audio integration roadmap item; do not merge audio callbacks until the RT gate covers them.

issues_identified.title: validate.yml still runs on ubuntu-22.04 only; no Windows MSVC gate yet
issues_identified.detail: The fork is a Windows/MSVC-first plugin in practice, but validate.yml runs on ubuntu-22.04 and only runs the JS copyright gate, the shell-based GPLv3/SPDX checks, and the Python RT-safety audit. There is no build gate in the current validate.yml, and no Windows runner. That is acceptable for the license/copyright/RT-safety gates, but it means the repo has no CI gate that exercises the actual C++ build on the target platform.
issues_identified.recommended_next: Add a build gate later when CI properly reflects the target toolchain. Not a release blocker for the current open-source plugin deliverable, but a roadmap item for release hygiene.

issues_identified.title: README.adoc, LICENSE-CHECK.md, and docs/LICENSE_AUDIT.md are slightly different voices of the same story
issues_identified.detail: Three documents now repeat the GPLv3+ status from different angles: the README §Licenses, LICENSE-CHECK.md, and docs/LICENSE_AUDIT.md. They agree on the substantive point, but they are not cross-linked, and the README still references upstream Xaymar/StreamFX URLs rather than the LibreCast Studio project identity consistently.
issues_identified.recommended_next: Add cross-links: README → LICENSE-CHECK.md → docs/LICENSE_AUDIT.md, and align the README project identity language with LibreCast Studio branding.

roadmap.vision: LibreCast Studio = community-facing open-source OBS plugin (GPLv3+), built on the nova-obs-fork codebase. The fork's StreamFX plugin layer is the initial public deliverable; the roadmap carries it from compliance-hardened source tree to a released, documented, CI-validated community plugin.

phases.goal: Lock the GPLv3+ identity and make the CI gates actually fail on the things they are meant to fail on.
milestones: A.1: SPDX header pass across all source/ files; local verify with validate.yml license-check job
A.2: Extend copyright.js or add a second CI step so SPDX-ID is enforced in depth
A.3: Reconcile lainon attribution: real git author vs. stale header; update AUTHORS.md/CREDITS if needed
A.4: Write project ADR recording the GPLv3 commercial-derivative blocker
phases.exit_criteria: license-check job fails on a file missing SPDX-ID in a throwaway PR; copyright gate is defensive in depth; AUTHORS.md/CREDITS reflects actual contributors; ADR committed

phases.phase: Phase B — Release Hygiene & Release Pipeline
phases.goal: Make the repo releasable as an open-source OBS plugin with a clean release artifact and a real build gate.
milestones: B.1: Add a Windows MSVC build gate to validate.yml (or a separate build workflow) so CI reflects the target platform
B.2: Define the release artifact shape: plugin .dll/.so, OBS asset bundle, release notes, GPL-3.0-or-later license copy, README, CREDITS
B.3: Create a release workflow or release checklist (tag, artifact, notes, asset upload) that can be executed on demand
B.4: Clean up README branding/language for LibreCast Studio; add cross-links to LICENSE-CHECK.md and docs/LICENSE_AUDIT.md
B.5: Verify submodule pin doc (SUBMODULE_PIN.md) stays current after any submodule update
phases.exit_criteria: A tagged release candidate can be produced from the repo with a documented, repeatable process; CI gates green on the release branch

phases.goal: Open the LibreCast Studio community surface and make the plugin discoverable to the OBS/streaming audience.
milestones: C.1: Publish the open-source plugin release to the LibreCast Studio GitHub org/repo with a clear README, license, and contribution guide
C.2: Write a landing narrative for LibreCast Studio: what it is, what the StreamFX plugin layer provides today, what the GPLv3+ boundary means for downstream users and commercial distributors
C.3: Prepare Discoverability assets: short description, tags, screenshot/media guidance, and a wiki/home page structure for the LibreCast Studio community
C.4: Define the community moderation + contribution posture for the LibreCast Studio guild (1542963701894877226): contribution path, issue templates, PR expectations, code-of-conduct baseline
C.5: Align the OBS Fork branding in the repo with the LibreCast Studio product name and guild identity
phases.exit_criteria: A public release is posted; the community guild has a documented contribution path and moderation baseline; the plugin is discoverable under the LibreCast Studio identity

phases.goal: Grow the plugin beyond the initial StreamFX layer only after the open-source base and GTM surface are stable.
milestones: D.1: Prioritize extension work that is compatible with GPLv3+ and useful to the OBS community, rather than proprietary Nexus features
D.2: If Nexus wants commercial OBS-adjacent capability, fund a separate clean-room effort per the ADR; do not merge it into this fork
D.3: Track RT-safety gate coverage as the audio/render surface grows; extend TARGET_FILES whenever a new real-time TU is added
phases.exit_criteria: Phase D is gated on Phase A-C exit criteria; no proprietary code path is merged into the fork
